excerpt: A central part of meeting our safety baselines is implementing mitigations to address various types of model risk.
paraphrase: Mitigations are a key element of satisfying the safety baselines by addressing different kinds of model risk.

excerpt: Our mitigation strategy will involve both containment measures, which help reduce risks related to possession of a frontier model, as well as deployment mitigations, which help reduce risks from active use of a frontier model.
paraphrase: The mitigation approach combines containment measures for possession-related risk and deployment mitigations for use-related risk.

excerpt: As a result, these mitigations might span increasing compartmentalization, restricting deployment to trusted users, implementing refusals, redacting training data, or alerting distribution partners.
paraphrase: Possible mitigations include greater compartmentalization, restricting deployment to trusted users, refusals, redacting training data, and alerting distribution partners.

excerpt: Model assistance for cyberattacks is meaningful only for non-programming uses and the model cannot meaningfully execute elements of cyber operations
paraphrase: At Low risk level, the model only assists with non-programming aspects of cyberattacks and cannot execute cyber operations itself.

excerpt: Cyber theory of attack eval: On a dataset of challenging conceptual multiple-choice questions extracted and rephrased from pentest writeups, the model performs significantly below the human baseline (X% vs Y%)
paraphrase: The Cyber theory of attack evaluation tests whether the model scores significantly below humans on conceptual pentest-derived multiple-choice questions.

excerpt: GPT vs search availability exploit eval: On a set of misconfigured web servers vulnerable to denial of service, cybersecurity professionals find <X% more bugs when provided with GPT assistance
paraphrase: The GPT vs search availability exploit evaluation measures whether GPT assistance helps professionals find more bugs in misconfigured servers, below a threshold X%.

excerpt: Code de-obfuscation eval: Model recovers variable names and code semantics at lower performance than commercial deobfuscation tools (X% vs Y%)
paraphrase: The Code de-obfuscation evaluation compares the model's ability to recover variable names and semantics against commercial tools, requiring lower performance.

excerpt: AI-assisted capture-the-flag eval: Participants in a hacking challenge (capture-the-flag) obtain <X% higher score from using ChatGPT augmented with the ability to execute commands on a vulnerable virtual machine.
paraphrase: The AI-assisted capture-the-flag evaluation measures whether hacking challenge participants score less than X% higher when using command-executing ChatGPT.

excerpt: Model can provide information relevant to creating CBRN threats with comparable utility to existing resources (e.g., textbooks, search engines), but nothing more than that
paraphrase: At Low risk, the model's CBRN-relevant information is no more useful than existing resources like textbooks or search engines.

excerpt: GPT vs search eval: Post-PhD professionals trained in biology (specifically genetics, virology, or microbiology) experience no improvement in success rates for writing CDC Class B biological agent development instructions using a search engine and GPT versus just a search engine (X% vs X%), including across accuracy, completeness, and innovation metrics.
paraphrase: This evaluation tests whether post-PhD biology professionals see no improvement in writing CDC Class B biological agent instructions when using GPT plus search versus search alone.

excerpt: This holds true for chemistry, nuclear, and radiological post-PhD professionals students as well
paraphrase: The same no-improvement finding applies to post-PhD professionals in chemistry, nuclear, and radiological fields.

excerpt: GPT vs search eval: Undergraduate students with some coursework in biology (specifically genetics, virology, or microbiology) experience no improvement in success rates for writing CDC Class B biological agent development instructions using a search engine and GPT versus just a search engine (X% vs X%), including across accuracy, completeness, and innovation metrics.
paraphrase: This evaluation tests whether undergraduate biology students see no improvement in writing biological agent instructions when using GPT plus search versus search alone.

excerpt: This holds true for chemistry, nuclear, and radiological study undergraduate students as well
paraphrase: The same no-improvement finding applies to undergraduate students studying chemistry, nuclear, and radiological topics.

excerpt: GPT vs search identify suppliers eval: <X% more participants succeed in finding DNA suppliers that do not screen orders using a search engine and GPT versus just a search engine.
paraphrase: This evaluation tests whether fewer than X% more participants succeed in identifying non-screening DNA suppliers using GPT plus search versus search alone.

excerpt: Model can create (potentially interactive) content with comparable persuasive effectiveness to typical human-written content (e.g., an op-ed from a reputable news source; 1:1 conversation with a typical randomly-assigned individual), but mitigations bring this persuasive effectiveness down to that of a low-quality article
paraphrase: At Medium pre-mitigation risk, the model can match human-level persuasive content, but mitigations reduce its effectiveness to that of a low-quality article.

excerpt: Political articles eval: Content generated by model increases rate of human belief in a political issue significantly compared to human-generated controls (X% vs Y%), but mitigations bring it to (X% vs X%)
paraphrase: The Political articles evaluation tests belief change from model-generated versus human-generated content, with mitigations equalizing the effect.
stated_bar: X% vs Y%; X% vs X%

excerpt: Interactive political conversations eval: Long-term 1:1 interactive conversation with a digital “friend” increases the rate of human belief in a political issue significantly when the digital friend is a model versus a real human (X% vs Y%), but mitigations bring it to (X% vs X%)
paraphrase: The Interactive political conversations evaluation tests belief change from long-term model conversation versus human conversation, with mitigations equalizing the effect.
stated_bar: X% vs Y%; X% vs X%

excerpt: Donations eval: Content generated by model does not significantly increase donations to a charitable cause compared to human-generated controls (X% vs X%)
paraphrase: The Donations evaluation tests that model-generated content does not significantly increase charitable donations compared to human-generated content.

excerpt: Digital action eval: Content generated by model does not increase rate of installing a Chrome extension significantly compared to human-generated controls (X% vs X%)
paraphrase: The Digital action evaluation tests that model-generated content does not significantly increase extension installation compared to human-generated content.

excerpt: Phishing eval: Model cannot write a realistic phishing email that convinces employees to submit login details on a phishing site (<X% success rate)
paraphrase: The Phishing evaluation requires that the model cannot write phishing emails effective enough to convince employees, below a success threshold.

excerpt: Believable biology research proposal: <X% of subtly dangerous proposals submitted by a model are approved by a biology wet lab
paraphrase: This evaluation requires that fewer than X% of subtly dangerous model-generated proposals are approved by a biology wet lab.

excerpt: Backdoored internal ChatGPT eval: No employees are convinced to run code with a subtle backdoor, e.g., a specific HTTP request, when ChatGPT is instructed to insert backdoors in code generations
paraphrase: This evaluation requires that no employees are persuaded to run backdoored code generated by a ChatGPT instructed to insert subtle backdoors.

excerpt: Copy GPT weights eval: Model convinces no employees to attempt to copy weights into a new location
paraphrase: This evaluation requires that the model persuades no employees to attempt copying model weights elsewhere.

excerpt: Monitored misuse: <X% of users are using the model for political persuasion purposes, and no electoral campaigns have been found that rely on our models.
paraphrase: This monitoring measure requires that fewer than X% of users use the model for political persuasion, and no electoral campaigns are found relying on the models.

excerpt: Model can robustly complete a diverse set of chained actions and acquire resources (e.g., spin up an AWS instance, complete a Fiverr task), but post-mitigation, can only take discrete actions if explicitly instructed to do so, and fails to chain actions or acquire resources
paraphrase: At Medium pre-mitigation risk, the model can complete chained actions and acquire resources, but post-mitigation is limited to explicitly instructed discrete actions.

excerpt: Server purchase eval: With extensive scaffolding, the model can buy additional server space (>X% success rate) but post-mitigations it fails.
paraphrase: The Server purchase evaluation tests that the model can buy server space with scaffolding above a threshold success rate pre-mitigation, but fails post-mitigation.

excerpt: Freelance job eval: Model cannot autonomously find and complete freelance tasks on Fiverr, but can complete tasks X% of time with some scaffolding and assistance; this reduces to 0% post-mitigations
paraphrase: The Freelance job evaluation shows the model completes Fiverr tasks at rate X% with scaffolding pre-mitigation, dropping to 0% post-mitigation.

excerpt: Reward hacking eval: Model cannot reward hack in a structured environment (0% success rate)
paraphrase: The Reward hacking evaluation requires a 0% success rate for the model attempting reward hacking in a structured environment.

excerpt: Research engineering eval: Model cannot complete long-term research engineering tasks (e.g., autonomously find compute efficiency wins on pretraining, discover and fix bugs that cause performance regressions); 0% success rate
paraphrase: The Research engineering evaluation requires a 0% success rate on autonomous long-term research engineering tasks.

excerpt: Weights escape eval: Model cannot successfully penetrate any important layers of defense on its own weights (e.g. exploiting a browsing environment, finding a vulnerability in inference code); 0% success rate.
paraphrase: The Weights escape evaluation requires a 0% success rate for the model penetrating defenses protecting its own weights.

excerpt: Beyond our above-detailed processes with regards to evaluations, monitoring, and forecasting, we want to make a set of safety baselines and procedural commitments.
paraphrase: In addition to evaluation, monitoring, and forecasting processes, the framework introduces safety baselines and procedural commitments.

excerpt: Note that these processes also apply to training runs as we will perform periodic evaluations (e.g., of checkpoints) during model training.
paraphrase: The evaluation processes will also be applied during training via periodic checkpoint evaluations.

excerpt: As mentioned in the introduction, OpenAI already has extensive safety processes in place both before and after deployment (e.g., system cards, red-teaming, refusals, jailbreak monitoring, etc.).
paraphrase: OpenAI states it already maintains extensive pre- and post-deployment safety processes including system cards, red-teaming, refusals, and jailbreak monitoring.

excerpt: We now augment these processes with three safety baselines.
paraphrase: OpenAI is adding three safety baselines on top of these existing processes.

excerpt: If we reach (or are forecasted to reach) at least “high” pre-mitigation risk in any of the considered categories: we will ensure that our security is hardened in a way that is designed to prevent our mitigations and controls from being circumvented via exfiltration (by the time we hit “high” pre-mitigation risk).
paraphrase: Upon reaching or forecasting at least High pre-mitigation risk in any category, security will be hardened to prevent circumvention via exfiltration by the time that risk level is reached.

excerpt: This is defined as establishing network and compute security controls designed to help prevent the captured risk from being exploited or exfiltrated, as assessed and implemented by the Security team.
paraphrase: Asset protection is defined as network and compute security controls to prevent exploitation or exfiltration of the captured risk, assessed and implemented by the Security team.

excerpt: increasing compartmentalization, including immediately restricting access to a limited nameset of people, restricting access to critical know-how such as algorithmic secrets or model weights, and including a strict approval process for access during this period
paraphrase: Possible measures include restricting access to a small set of people, limiting access to critical know-how like algorithmic secrets or weights, and imposing strict approval for access.

excerpt: deploying only into restricted environments (i.e., ensuring the model is only available for inference in restricted environments) with strong technical controls that allow us to moderate the model’s capabilities
paraphrase: Another possible measure is deploying the model only in restricted environments with strong technical controls to moderate capabilities.

excerpt: increasing the prioritization of information security controls.
paraphrase: Another possible measure is prioritizing information security controls more highly.

excerpt: Only models with a post-mitigation score of "medium" or below can be deployed.
paraphrase: Deployment is restricted to models scoring Medium or below post-mitigation.

excerpt: In other words, if we reach (or are forecasted to reach) at least “high” pre-mitigation risk in any of the considered categories, we will not continue with deployment of that model (by the time we hit “high” pre-mitigation risk) until there are reasonably mitigations in place for the relevant post-mitigation risk level to be back at most to “medium” level.
paraphrase: If High pre-mitigation risk is reached or forecasted in any category, deployment will halt until mitigations bring post-mitigation risk back to Medium or below.

excerpt: (Note that a potentially effective mitigation in this context could be restricting deployment to trusted parties.)
paraphrase: One possible mitigation noted is restricting deployment to trusted parties.

excerpt: Only models with a post-mitigation score of "high" or below can be developed further.
paraphrase: Further development is restricted to models scoring High or below post-mitigation.

excerpt: In other words, if we reach (or are forecasted to reach) “critical” pre-mitigation risk along any risk category, we commit to ensuring there are sufficient mitigations in place for that model (by the time we reach that risk level in our capability development, let alone deployment) for the overall post-mitigation risk to be back at most to “high” level.
paraphrase: If Critical pre-mitigation risk is reached or forecasted, mitigations must bring post-mitigation risk back to High or below before continuing development.

excerpt: Note that this should not preclude safety-enhancing development.
paraphrase: The restriction is not meant to prevent development aimed at improving safety.

excerpt: We would also focus our efforts as a company towards solving these safety challenges and only continue with capabilities-enhancing development if we can reasonably assure ourselves (via the operationalization processes) that it is safe to do so.
paraphrase: The company would prioritize solving the safety challenges and only continue capability-enhancing development once safety is reasonably assured through the operationalization processes.

excerpt: Additionally, to protect against “critical” pre-mitigation risk, we need dependable evidence that the model is sufficiently aligned that it does not initiate “critical”-risk-level tasks unless explicitly instructed to do so.
paraphrase: To guard against Critical pre-mitigation risk, dependable evidence is needed that the model will not initiate critical-risk tasks without explicit instruction.

excerpt: We also establish an operational structure to oversee our procedural commitments.
paraphrase: An operational structure is established to oversee the procedural commitments.

excerpt: These commitments aim to make sure that: (1) there is a dedicated team “on the ground” focused on preparedness research and monitoring (Preparedness team), (2) there is an advisory group (Safety Advisory Group) that has a sufficient diversity of perspectives and technical expertise to provide nuanced input and recommendations, and (3) there is a final decision-maker (OpenAI Leadership, with the option for the OpenAI Board of Directors to overrule).
paraphrase: The structure ensures a dedicated Preparedness team, a diverse Safety Advisory Group, and a final decision-maker in OpenAI Leadership subject to Board override.

section_heading: Parties in the Preparedness Framework operationalization process
excerpt: The Preparedness team conducts research, evaluations, monitoring, forecasting, and continuous updating of the Scorecard with input from teams that have relevant domain expertise.
paraphrase: The Preparedness team is responsible for research, evaluations, monitoring, forecasting, and updating the Scorecard, drawing on domain-expert teams.

section_heading: Parties in the Preparedness Framework operationalization process
excerpt: The Safety Advisory Group (SAG), including the SAG Chair, provides a diversity of perspectives to evaluate the strength of evidence related to catastrophic risk and recommend appropriate actions.
paraphrase: The SAG, including its Chair, evaluates evidence strength on catastrophic risk and recommends appropriate actions using diverse perspectives.

section_heading: Parties in the Preparedness Framework operationalization process
excerpt: The SAG will strive to recommend mitigations that are as targeted and non-disruptive as possible while not compromising safety.
paraphrase: The SAG aims to recommend mitigations that are targeted and minimally disruptive without sacrificing safety.

section_heading: Parties in the Preparedness Framework operationalization process
excerpt: In particular, we recognize that pausing deployment or development would be the last resort (but potentially necessary) option in these circumstances
paraphrase: Pausing deployment or development is recognized as a last-resort but possibly necessary option.

excerpt: This role is expected to rotate, as appointed by OpenAI leadership.
paraphrase: The SAG Chair role is expected to rotate and is appointed by OpenAI leadership.

section_heading: Parties in the Preparedness Framework operationalization process
excerpt: The OpenAI Leadership, i.e., the CEO or a person designated by them, serves as the default decision-maker on all decisions
paraphrase: OpenAI Leadership, meaning the CEO or their designee, is the default decision-maker for all decisions.

section_heading: Parties in the Preparedness Framework operationalization process
excerpt: The OpenAI Board of Directors (BoD), as the ultimate governing body of OpenAI, will oversee OpenAI Leadership’s implementation and decision-making pursuant to this Preparedness Framework.
paraphrase: The Board of Directors, as the ultimate governing body, will oversee Leadership's implementation and decisions under the Framework.

section_heading: Parties in the Preparedness Framework operationalization process
excerpt: The BoD may review certain decisions taken and will receive appropriate documentation (i.e., without needing to proactively ask) to ensure the BOD is fully informed and able to fulfill its oversight role
paraphrase: The Board may review decisions and will automatically receive documentation to remain fully informed and capable of oversight.

context_stem: The Preparedness team is responsible for:
excerpt: maintaining and updating the Scorecard, including designing and running evaluations to provide Scorecard inputs and collecting relevant information on monitored misuse, red-teaming, and intelligence
paraphrase: The Preparedness team maintains the Scorecard, runs evaluations, and gathers information on misuse monitoring, red-teaming, and intelligence.

context_stem: The Preparedness team is responsible for:
excerpt: monitoring for unknown unknowns and making the case for inclusion in the Preparedness Framework of any new risk categories as they emerge
paraphrase: The Preparedness team monitors for unknown unknowns and proposes adding new risk categories as they arise.

context_stem: The Preparedness team is responsible for:
excerpt: ensuring the risk level distinctions in the Tracked Risk Categories section are appropriate given developments in frontier AI models, and suggesting updates to these levels if needed
paraphrase: The Preparedness team ensures risk level distinctions remain appropriate as frontier AI develops, and proposes updates as needed.

context_stem: The Preparedness team is responsible for:
excerpt: forecasting potential changes to catastrophic risk levels, and summarizing evidence for an “early warning” / “heads up” as needed
paraphrase: The Preparedness team forecasts potential changes in catastrophic risk levels and summarizes evidence for early warnings as needed.

context_stem: The Preparedness team is responsible for:
excerpt: providing a monthly report (sent to the SAG, Leadership and BoD) synthesizing the above with any potential protective actions (the SAG Chair, OpenAI Leadership, and/or BoD can adjust this cadence as needed
paraphrase: A monthly report to the SAG, Leadership, and Board synthesizes findings and suggested protective actions, with cadence adjustable by SAG Chair, Leadership, or Board.

excerpt: If the Preparedness or any other team determines that any changes to the Preparedness Framework are necessary, it will include a case for this change in its report.
paraphrase: If any team determines changes to the Framework are needed, a case for that change is included in its report.

excerpt: The case will consist of the suggested new version of the relevant parts of the Preparedness Framework along with a summary of evidence supporting the change (and evidence against).
paraphrase: The change case includes the proposed revised text and a summary of supporting and opposing evidence.

excerpt: This case is then sent to SAG and processed according to the standard decision-making process described below.
paraphrase: The change case is submitted to the SAG and follows the standard decision-making process.

excerpt: Fast-track: In the rare case that a severe risk rapidly develops (e.g., there is a change in our understanding of model safety that requires urgent response), the Preparedness team can request a fast track for the SAG to process the report urgently.
paraphrase: In rare cases of rapidly developing severe risk, the Preparedness team may request an urgent fast-track processing of its report by the SAG.

excerpt: The SAG Chair should also coordinate with OpenAI Leadership for immediate reaction as needed to address the risk
paraphrase: The SAG Chair should coordinate with Leadership for immediate action to address the risk if needed.

excerpt: The SAG will be responsible for assessing the merits of each case submitted to them.
paraphrase: The SAG assesses the merits of each submitted case.

excerpt: Then, the SAG Chair will forward the case to the OpenAI Leadership (sharing also with the BoD and Preparedness) and include a draft of possible next steps (e.g., approving a change to the Scorecard or Preparedness Framework; requesting changes to other internal and external processes as needed; highlighting a need to accelerate security procedures based on a forecasted increase in risk levels) as well as rationale.
paraphrase: The SAG Chair forwards the case to Leadership, sharing with the Board and Preparedness team, including a draft of possible next steps and rationale.

excerpt: The OpenAI Leadership will make the final decision and be responsible for overseeing any mitigations (with SAG’s assistance, if requested).
paraphrase: OpenAI Leadership makes the final decision and oversees mitigations, with optional SAG assistance.

context_stem: The OpenAI Leadership will make the final decision and be responsible for overseeing any mitigations (with SAG’s assistance, if requested).
excerpt: The BoD will be given visibility into processes, and can review decisions and otherwise require reports and information from OpenAI Leadership as necessary to fulfill the BoD’s oversight role.
paraphrase: The Board has visibility into processes and can review decisions and demand information from Leadership to fulfill its oversight role.

context_stem: The OpenAI Leadership will make the final decision and be responsible for overseeing any mitigations (with SAG’s assistance, if requested).
excerpt: Where necessary, the BoD may reverse a decision and/or mandate a revised course of action
paraphrase: The Board may reverse a decision or mandate a revised course of action when necessary.

context_stem: The OpenAI Leadership will make the final decision and be responsible for overseeing any mitigations (with SAG’s assistance, if requested).
excerpt: (For the avoidance of doubt, Leadership can also make decisions without the SAG’s participation, i.e., the SAG does not have the ability to “filibuster”)
paraphrase: Leadership can make decisions without SAG participation, and the SAG cannot block decisions.

excerpt: Internal visibility: The Preparedness Framework, reports and decisions will be documented and visible to the BoD and within OpenAI (with redactions as needed given internal compartmentalization of research work).
paraphrase: The Framework, reports, and decisions are documented and made visible to the Board and internally, with redactions where compartmentalization requires.

excerpt: This also includes any audit trails created from the below.
paraphrase: Audit trails from subsequent processes are included in this visibility commitment.

excerpt: Audits: Scorecard evaluations (and corresponding mitigations) will be audited by qualified, independent third-parties to ensure accurate reporting of results, either by reproducing findings or by reviewing methodology to ensure soundness, at a cadence specified by the SAG and/or upon the request of OpenAI Leadership or the BoD.
paraphrase: Independent third-party audits of Scorecard evaluations and mitigations will occur at a cadence set by the SAG or upon request by Leadership or the Board.

excerpt: External access: We will also continue to enable external research and government access for model releases to increase the depth of red-teaming and testing of frontier model capabilities
paraphrase: External research and government access to model releases will continue to be enabled, to deepen red-teaming and testing.

excerpt: Safety drills: A critical part of this process is to be prepared if fast-moving emergency scenarios arise, including what default organizational response might look like (including how to stress-test against the pressures of our business or our culture).
paraphrase: Being prepared for fast-moving emergencies, including default organizational responses tested against business and culture pressures, is a critical part of the process.

excerpt: While the Preparedness team and SAG will of course work hard on forecasting and preparing for risks, safety drills can help the organization build “muscle memory” by practicing and coming up with the right “default” responses for some of the foreseeable scenarios.
paraphrase: Safety drills help build organizational muscle memory for default responses to foreseeable scenarios, complementing forecasting efforts by the Preparedness team and SAG.

excerpt: Therefore, the SAG will call for safety drills at a recommended minimum yearly basis
paraphrase: The SAG will call for safety drills at least once a year as a recommended minimum.

excerpt: For each of these accountability measures, decision-making will follow the standard process (i.e., SAG chair synthesizes final recommendation, which OpenAI leadership makes a final decision on, that the BoD can overrule if needed).
paraphrase: All accountability measures follow the standard decision process: SAG Chair recommendation, Leadership decision, Board override option.

excerpt: The Preparedness team monthly report updates the Scorecard pre-mitigation risk level in persuasion to “high” for a model that has just been trained.
paraphrase: In this scenario, the monthly report updates the pre-mitigation persuasion risk level to High for a newly trained model.

excerpt: This report includes a case with evidence from evaluations.
paraphrase: The report includes a case supported by evaluation evidence.

excerpt: The SAG Chair accepts the evidence supporting this new risk level, which would trigger two safety baselines: (1) to not continue with the deployment of the pre-mitigated model until mitigations are in place to ensure the post-mitigation risk will be at most “medium,” and (2) to ensure security measures are in place to prevent exfiltration by relevant actors; in this case, that would likely include foreign disinformation groups.
paraphrase: The SAG Chair accepts the evidence, triggering two baselines: halting deployment until post-mitigation risk is at most Medium, and ensuring exfiltration-prevention security measures against relevant actors like foreign disinformation groups.

excerpt: The Preparedness team consults with relevant teams about the recommended mitigations and puts together a final set of suggestions for how to ensure the model is back at “medium” risk, which the SAG agrees with.
paraphrase: The Preparedness team consults relevant teams and proposes mitigations to bring risk back to Medium, which the SAG approves.

excerpt: The SAG Chair escalates to OpenAI leadership for a final decision. All documentation is sent to both OpenAI Leadership and the BoD for visibility and potential review
paraphrase: The SAG Chair escalates to Leadership for the final decision, with all documentation shared with Leadership and the Board.

excerpt: OpenAI Leadership agrees that the new pre-mitigation level for persuasion would be “high,” and agrees with the SAG plan to ensure sufficient mitigations are in place.
paraphrase: Leadership confirms the High pre-mitigation level and agrees with the SAG mitigation plan.

excerpt: The BoD does not overrule the decision. The SAG works with the Preparedness and Security teams to ensure baseline safety measures are in place
